syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Exploring Society India and Beyond Part-I

concepts.learning_objective: Identify India's neighbours and explain why the region is called the Indian Subcontinent.
Describe the natural features that mark India's limits and their role in shaping its climate, culture and history.
Explain how the Himalayas were formed by India's collision with Eurasia and why they are still rising.
Distinguish between the Himadri, Himachal and Shivalik ranges of the Himalayas.
Explain why the Himalayas are called the 'Water Tower of Asia'.
Explain why Ladakh is a cold desert and how its rugged terrain and salty lakes formed.
Identify the wildlife, animals and cultural life of Ladakh and the Himalayan region.
Explain how Himalayan rivers make the Gangetic Plains fertile and important for agriculture.
Explain why the flat Northern Plains support a large population, transport networks and civilisation.

topics.title: The Thar Desert and the Aravalli Hills

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Thar Desert's dunes and harsh conditions and how its people have adapted to water scarcity.
Describe the age, minerals and role of the Aravalli Hills in north-western India.
Explain what a plateau and a peninsula are and why southern India is called a peninsular plateau.
Compare the Western and Eastern Ghats and explain the direction of flow of the plateau's rivers.
Describe the plateau's minerals, forests, waterfalls and tribal communities and their importance.
Distinguish between the West Coast and the East Coast of India and their landforms.
Explain how deltas form and why the eastern deltas are fertile.
Describe the Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar island groups and their importance.

topics.title: The Sundarbans and the hills of the Northeast

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the location and unique features of the Sundarbans delta.
Describe the Meghalaya Plateau's hills, heavy rainfall and eco-friendly ways of life.

topics.title: Weather, the atmosphere and the elements of weather

concepts.learning_objective: Define weather as the state of the atmosphere at a particular time and place and describe the atmosphere.
Describe the troposphere as the lowest layer of the atmosphere where almost all weather occurs and explain why its thickness varies.
Identify the five elements of weather and explain why they must be measured using common standards.

topics.title: Reading Nature's clues and the science of meteorology
topics.ncert_sections: Weather and its Elements (Observing Nature's clues)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how traditional observations of plants and animals have been used to forecast rain and storms.
Describe meteorology as the systematic study of weather that forms the basis of forecasting.
Describe how thermometers work and why digital thermometers are increasingly preferred.
Calculate the range of temperature and the mean daily temperature from recorded data.
Identify rain, snow, sleet and hail as forms of precipitation.
Explain how a rain gauge measures rainfall in millimetres and where it should be placed.
Explain why atmospheric pressure and available oxygen decrease at higher altitudes.
Use barometer readings in millibars to recognise normal pressure and a depression.
Describe wind as air moving from high to low pressure and explain why its speed and direction matter.
Distinguish the uses of the wind vane, wind sock and anemometer.
Interpret relative humidity values and relate them to evaporation, drying and sweating.
Identify the hygrometer and explain why industries and museums monitor humidity.

topics.title: Weather stations and predicting the weather

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how weather stations and Automated Weather Stations bring instruments together to record weather data.
Explain how weather predictions and graded warnings help people and governments prepare for extreme weather.
Distinguish weather (day-to-day conditions) from climate (the long-term pattern over decades).
Explain how seasons, including India's rainy season and the six traditional ritus, relate to weather and climate.
Identify the main climate types of India's regions, from alpine to arid and tropical.
Relate the climate of a region to the crops grown and the way people live there.

topics.title: Latitude and Altitude
topics.ncert_sections: Factors Determining the Climate: (a) Latitude, (b) Altitude

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why places at low latitudes are warmer than places at high latitudes.
Explain why temperature decreases as altitude increases, using hill stations as examples.

topics.title: Sea, Winds, Topography and Microclimates
topics.ncert_sections: Factors Determining the Climate: (c) Proximity to the sea, (d) Winds, (e) Topography; Putting it all together

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how nearness to the sea moderates temperature and narrows its range.
Describe how winds and landforms such as mountains bring or block heat, cold and moisture.
Define a microclimate and give examples such as valleys, forests and urban heat islands.
Explain how unequal heating of land and ocean creates pressure differences that drive the monsoon winds.
Describe the advance of the southwest monsoon and the winter northeast monsoon over India.
Recognise traditional local knowledge used to predict the monsoon.

topics.title: Climate, our Lives and Disasters
topics.ncert_sections: Climate and our Lives; Climates and Disasters

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how climate shapes festivals, agriculture and the economy, including the effects of monsoon failure.
Describe how cyclones form and how they affect India's coasts.
Explain the natural and human causes of floods, landslides and forest fires.
Identify the human activities that have driven climate change since the 19th century.
Explain the natural greenhouse effect and how extra greenhouse gases cause global warming.
Evaluate climate mitigation measures and the challenges they face.
Explain what disappeared when the Harappan 'First Urbanisation' disintegrated.
Describe when and where India's 'Second Urbanisation' began and how we know about it.
State the meaning of 'janapada' and how janapadas formed around clans.
Identify the sixteen mahajanapadas, their capitals and why many lay in the Ganga plains.
Describe the defensive features of mahajanapada capitals.
Explain the role of the sabha or samiti in advising and checking the raja.
Describe how monarchical mahajanapadas were ruled.
Explain why the ganas or sanghas such as Vajji and Malla are called early republics.
Explain how iron tools and weapons shaped the Second Urbanisation.
Describe the first Indian coins and why growing trade needed them.
Distinguish between jati and varna and identify the roles of the four varnas.
Explain how the varna-jati system was flexible earlier and became rigid over time.
Identify the Uttarapatha and Dakshinapatha and the role of roads in connecting regions.
Describe the rise of cities and kingdoms in eastern and southern India.

topics.title: What is an Empire? Meaning and features
topics.ncert_sections: What is an Empire?; Features of an empire

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of 'empire' and the Sanskrit titles used for an emperor.
Describe how tributary kingdoms related to an emperor through tribute and loyalty.
Identify the main functions of an emperor and the reasons kings expanded kingdoms into empires.
Explain why production and trade were key to maintaining an empire.
Identify the major ancient trade routes and traded goods of the Subcontinent.
Describe the organisation and autonomy of guilds (shrenis) in ancient India.

topics.title: The Rise of Magadha and the Nandas

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the geographical and economic factors behind the rise of Magadha.
Describe the rise of the Nanda dynasty and the reasons for its fall.

topics.title: The Arrival of the Greeks
topics.ncert_sections: The Arrival of the Greeks; Alexander's dialogue with the Gymnosophists

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Alexander's campaign in northwest India, its end and its impact.
Explain who satraps were and how Porus was treated after his defeat.
Interpret the meeting between Alexander and the Indian sages called Gymnosophists.

topics.title: The Mighty Mauryas: Chandragupta and Kautilya
topics.ncert_sections: The Mighty Mauryas; The story of Kautilya; Kautilya's concept of a kingdom

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Chandragupta Maurya founded and expanded the Maurya Empire.
Identify the seven parts (saptanga) of a kingdom described in the Arthashastra.
Interpret Kautilya's view that a king's welfare lies in the welfare of his subjects.

topics.title: The King Who Chose Peace: Ashoka

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Kalinga war changed Ashoka's path.
Describe the language, script and messages of Ashoka's edicts.
Evaluate Ashoka's efforts for the welfare of his subjects and the fairness of his officials.

topics.title: Life in the Mauryan period and Mauryan contributions
topics.ncert_sections: Life in the Mauryan period; Some Contributions of the Mauryas

concepts.learning_objective: Describe city life, agriculture and food security in the Mauryan period.
Identify Mauryan art and architecture and its legacy in modern India's symbols.
Explain the causes that led parts of an empire to break away.
Evaluate why empires are described as a paradox of unity and force.

topics.title: Breakup of the Maurya empire and the age of reorganisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Maurya empire broke up around 185 BCE and what followed.
Describe why the post-Maurya period is called the age of reorganisation and place it on a timeline.
Identify the peaceful and forceful ways in which the new kingdoms gained control.
Describe the Shunga dynasty founded by Pushyamitra Shunga and the ashvamedha yajna.
Identify Shunga contributions to literature, art and architecture such as the Bharhut Stupa.
Describe the extent of the Satavahana kingdom and its agriculture and trade networks.
Explain features of life under the Satavahanas, including naming traditions, inscriptions and patronage.
Describe King Kharavela of Kalinga and what the Hathigumpha inscription records.
Explain why the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves are examples of rock-cut architecture.

topics.title: Kingdoms and life in the South

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Sangam literature and the themes of the epic Silappadikaram.
Explain the achievements of the Chola king Karikala, including the Grand Anicut.
Describe the capitals, trade and importance of the Chera and Pandya kingdoms.

topics.title: Invasions of the Indo-Greeks and the Shakas

concepts.learning_objective: Explain who the Indo-Greeks were and how they were influenced by Indian culture.
Use the Shaka Samvat calendar and relate it to the Gregorian calendar.

topics.title: The emergence of the Kushanas and cultural confluence

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Kushana empire, King Kanishka and the values shown on his coins.
Distinguish between the Gandhara and Mathura schools of art.
Evaluate how cultural exchange in this period led to a blend with a dominance of Indian themes.

chapters.title: The Gupta Era: An Age of Tireless Creativity

topics.title: The Iron Pillar and a new power emerges

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Iron Pillar of Delhi, its date and why it has not rusted.
Explain how the Guptas rose to power as the Kushana Empire weakened.
Identify Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) and distinguish him from other rulers named Chandragupta.

topics.title: The warrior king Samudragupta and the extent of the empire

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what the Prayaga prashasti and coins tell us about Samudragupta.
Identify the regions of the Gupta Empire named in literary sources and on the map.

topics.title: A traveller's account of society in the Gupta age
topics.ncert_sections: A Traveller's Account of Indian Society in the Gupta Age

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Faxian's journey and the features of Gupta society he recorded.
Evaluate a traveller's account as one perspective that must be checked against other sources.

topics.title: Governance, administration and trade
topics.ncert_sections: Glimpses of the Gupta Empire: Governance and administration; New kings ... new titles; Thriving trade

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how titles and matrimonial alliances, such as that of Prabhavati Gupta, strengthened Gupta power.
Explain the Gupta system of provinces and land grants recorded on copper plates.
Describe the sources of Gupta revenue and the Indian Ocean trade network.

topics.title: New ideas and wonders: the classical age
topics.ncert_sections: New Ideas and Wonders: The Classical Age

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why peace, stability and royal patronage led to the 'classical age'.
Describe the contributions of Aryabhata and Varahamihira to mathematics and astronomy.
Describe Kalidasa's Meghadutam and the codification of Ayurveda in the Gupta period.

topics.title: The quest for beauty: Gupta art

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the major centres of Gupta art such as Sarnath, Ajanta, Udayagiri and Deogarh.
Interpret attributes such as vahanas to identify deities in Gupta sculpture.

topics.title: Decline of the Guptas and kingdoms of the south and northeast
topics.ncert_sections: The Decline of the Guptas; Meanwhile in the South and Northeast ...

concepts.learning_objective: State the causes of the decline of the Gupta Empire.
Describe the Pallava and Kamarupa kingdoms and Samudragupta's policy towards them.
Explain what sacredness means and that it can belong to a place, a journey, a route or the land itself.
Identify sacred places of different religions in India and why they are revered.
Explain the meaning of tirtha and the two-fold nature of a tirthayatra.
Describe Jain tirthas and the meaning of difficult hilltop pilgrimages such as Sabarimala.
Explain the perception of a divine presence in all of Nature, including Mother Earth as Bhudevi.
Describe how tribal communities and states protect sacred hills, peaks and other natural sites.
Describe pilgrimage networks such as the char dham, the 12 jyotirlingas and the 51 Shakti pithas.
Explain how travel along converging routes contributed to the cultural integration of the Subcontinent.

topics.title: Sacred ecology: rivers, Kumbh Mela and mountains
topics.ncert_sections: Sacred Ecology; Rivers and sangams; Kumbh Mela; Mountains and Forests

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how rivers have been revered in India since Vedic times.
Recall the legend and the four places of the Kumbh Mela and interpret its scale.
Explain why many tirthas are located on mountains and hilltops.
Identify the peepul as a tree sacred to several Indian traditions.
Explain what sacred groves are and how they help conserve biodiversity and water.
Explain how local legends about the epics' heroes linked diverse communities to the epics.
Explain why pilgrimage routes and trade routes often overlapped.
Identify the Uttarapatha and Dakshinapatha trade routes of ancient India.

topics.title: Sacred geography beyond India and conserving the sacred
topics.ncert_sections: Sacred Geography beyond India; Restoring and conserving the sacred

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that sacred geography exists in other cultures, such as among the Maoris.
Evaluate the need to protect sacred places from pollution and neglect.

chapters.title: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments

topics.title: What is Government and its Functions
topics.ncert_sections: What is Government? What are its Functions?; What is Democracy?; Functions of Government

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the roles of government, including Kautilya's three duties of a ruler.
Explain through the school committee example why choosing representatives is a democratic method.
Distinguish the legislative, executive and judicial functions of government.
Identify who or what gives a government its authority in different types of government.
Describe how governments are formed in democracies and in kingdoms.
Compare governments by their parts, their constitution and the goals they work for.

topics.title: Fundamental Principles of Democracy
topics.ncert_sections: Democratic Governments around the World; Fundamental principles of democracy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain equality, freedom and representative participation as principles of democracy.
Explain universal adult franchise and how it evolved in different democracies.
Explain the role of fundamental rights and an independent judiciary in a democracy.

topics.title: Forms of Democratic Government
topics.ncert_sections: Different forms of democratic governments; Table 9.1

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish direct democracy from representative democracy.
Distinguish parliamentary democracy from presidential democracy.
Describe the executive, the legislature with its two houses, and separation of power.

topics.title: A Peek into History: Early Republics and Rajadharma
topics.ncert_sections: A Peek into History; Other Forms of Government: Monarchy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Vajji mahajanapada and other ancient states are called early republics.
Describe what the Uttaramerur inscriptions reveal about elections to the village sabha.
Explain how rajadharma limited the power of kings in many parts of India.
Distinguish an absolute monarchy from a constitutional monarchy.
Describe a theocracy with the examples given in the chapter.
Describe dictatorship and oligarchy and recognise their signs.
Compare democracy with other forms of government on rights and freedoms.
Explain how elections keep a democratic government accountable.
Identify challenges that can hurt the ideals of democracy.

chapters.title: The Constitution of India — An Introduction

topics.title: What Is a Constitution and Why Do We Need One?
topics.ncert_sections: What Is a Constitution?; Why do we need a constitution?

concepts.learning_objective: Describe a constitution as the document that lays down a nation's basic principles, laws, organs of government, rights and duties.
Explain, using the rulebook analogy, why a country needs a constitution that everyone, including top officials, agrees to follow.

topics.title: Writing the Constitution of India
topics.ncert_sections: Writing the Constitution of India; How was our Constitution developed?

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the formation, membership and diversity of the Constituent Assembly.
Recall when the Constitution was adopted and when it came into effect, and link this to Republic Day.
Identify the role of the Drafting Committee and its chairman, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

topics.title: What Shaped and Influenced the Indian Constitution?
topics.ncert_sections: What Shaped and Influenced the Indian Constitution?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the ideals and experience of the freedom movement were carried into the Constitution.
Relate principles from India's civilisational heritage, such as the emphasis on duties, to features of the Constitution.
Identify ideas the Constitution makers drew from the constitutions of other countries.

topics.title: Key Features of the Constitution of India
topics.ncert_sections: Key Features of the Constitution of India

concepts.learning_objective: State the roles of the legislature, executive and judiciary as laid down in the Constitution.
Distinguish Fundamental Rights from Fundamental Duties with examples.
Explain why the Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the government rather than rights enforceable in court.

topics.title: The Constitution Is a Living Document
topics.ncert_sections: The Constitution is a Living Document

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that the Constitution can be changed through amendments that are carefully debated.
Give examples of how the Constitution and its interpretation have changed over time.
Recall that the original Constitution was handwritten and illustrated as a work of art.

topics.title: Understanding the Preamble
topics.ncert_sections: Understanding the Preamble: The Guiding Values of the Constitution of India

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of the key terms of the Preamble and how some were added later.
Apply the values of the Preamble to situations from everyday life.
Explain what the barter system is and how money differs from a barter commodity.
Identify the commodities and objects that different societies used in exchange before modern money.

topics.title: Why do we need money? Limitations of barter

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the problem of double coincidence of wants in barter.
Explain why the lack of a common standard measure of value made barter difficult.
Distinguish the problems of divisibility, portability and durability in barter.
Describe the Junbeel Mela of Assam as a barter fair that continues today.
Recognise everyday examples of barter such as book swaps and old clothes for utensils.
Explain how money works as a common medium of exchange.
Explain money as a store of value and a standard of deferred payment.
Explain how money measures value and allows goods to be compared through prices.
Describe the features of ancient Indian coins such as karshapanas or panas.
Explain how coinage helped trade across kingdoms and India's maritime trade.
Recall facts about later Indian coins, the anna and the rupee symbol.

topics.title: Paper money and new forms of money

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why paper money came into use and the role of the RBI in issuing currency.
Describe digital money such as UPI, QR code payments and debit or credit cards.
Identify a market and its essential features: buyers, sellers and an agreed price.
Distinguish between needs and wants in economics.
Describe the Hampi Bazaar of the Vijayanagara Empire as an example of a prosperous historical market.
Explain price as the amount agreed by a buyer and a seller, often reached through bargaining.
Explain how the quantities offered by sellers and required by buyers shape the price over time.

topics.title: Markets Around Us
topics.ncert_sections: Markets Around Us: Physical and online markets; Domestic and international markets

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish physical markets from online markets and their uses.
Distinguish domestic markets from international markets involving imports and exports.
Trace the flow of goods from producers through wholesalers and retailers to consumers.
Explain the roles of distributors in physical markets and aggregators in online markets.
Describe the chain of supply in the Surat textile market and the role of its wholesalers.

topics.title: The Role of Markets in People's Lives
topics.ncert_sections: The Role of Markets in People's Lives; How markets benefit society

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how markets help people access goods and services they cannot produce themselves.
Explain how consumer demand signals producers and benefits society.
Describe the social and cultural significance of markets, such as Ima Keithal.
Explain why the government sets maximum and minimum prices and minimum wages.
Explain how the government protects consumers through quality, safety and weights-and-measures rules.
Explain how the government mitigates harmful effects of markets and provides public goods.

topics.title: How Consumers Assess Quality
topics.ncert_sections: How can consumers assess the quality of products and services?

concepts.learning_objective: Identify certification marks such as FSSAI, ISI, AGMARK and BEE star ratings and what they indicate.
Use the information on a product label to judge a product before buying.
Evaluate reputation and reviews alongside certification marks when choosing a product.
